The Industrial Revolution, which began in the late 18th century, was a period of profound economic and technological transformation. Originating in Great Britain, it rapidly spread to other parts of Europe and North America. This era marked the shift from agrarian economies to industrialized and urbanized societies. Key inventions such as the steam engine, spinning jenny, and power loom revolutionized production processes, leading to significant advancements in manufacturing and transportation. However, the benefits of industrialization were not evenly distributed.
